accepted.s: The Palermo Protocol, adopted in 2000, is formally known as the:
o: UN Protocol on the Rights of Migrant Workers
UN Protocol on Transnational Organised Crime Investigations
UN Convention on the Elimination of Violence against Women
UN Protocol to Prevent, Suppress and Punish Trafficking in Persons, Especially Women and Children
accepted.x: The Palermo Protocol is the UN Protocol to Prevent, Suppress and Punish Trafficking in Persons, Especially Women and Children.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact official title rather than a similar human-rights instrument.
accepted.sec: Trafficking - UNODC report, Palermo Protocol, ITPA, Trafficking of Persons Bill 2018/2021  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Palermo Protocol:
1. It supplements the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime.
2. India has ratified it.
3. It deals specifically with trafficking in persons, especially women and children.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Palermo Protocol supplements the UNTOC and addresses trafficking in persons, particularly women and children; India has ratified it.
accepted.tq: Check each statement against the instrument’s purpose, legal relationship and ratification status.
accepted.sec: Trafficking - UNODC report, Palermo Protocol, ITPA, Trafficking of Persons Bill 2018/2021  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956, which of the following is correct?
o: Prostitution itself is treated as a crime in every circumstance.
Only trafficking of children is punishable.
Brothel-keeping, pimping, soliciting and living on the earnings of prostitution are punishable acts.
The Act abolishes protective homes maintained by State Governments.
accepted.x: The ITPA does not treat prostitution per se as a crime, but penalises activities such as brothel-keeping, pimping, soliciting and living on prostitution earnings.
accepted.tq: Use the distinction between the activity itself and associated exploitative activities.
accepted.sec: Trafficking - UNODC report, Palermo Protocol, ITPA, Trafficking of Persons Bill 2018/2021  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is associated with the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956?
o: Protective homes maintained by the States
National Investigation Agency as the sole investigating agency
Abolition of all State rehabilitation institutions
accepted.x: The ITPA provides for protective homes maintained by the States. The other alternatives are not features stated in relation to the Act.
accepted.tq: Match the statute with its institutional feature and reject unrelated enforcement measures.
accepted.sec: Trafficking - UNODC report, Palermo Protocol, ITPA, Trafficking of Persons Bill 2018/2021  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under Section 143 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which principle applies to trafficking?
o: Consent is relevant only if the trafficking is inter-State.
The victim’s consent is always a complete defence.
Consent matters only when the victim is an adult male.
accepted.x: Section 143 of the BNS treats the victim’s consent as immaterial in determining the offence of trafficking.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between consent as a defence and the statutory rule that consent is immaterial.
accepted.sec: Trafficking - UNODC report, Palermo Protocol, ITPA, Trafficking of Persons Bill 2018/2021  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was a feature of the Trafficking of Persons Bill, 2018?
o: It limited shelters to private institutions only.
It was enacted by both Houses without lapse.
It removed all provisions relating to rehabilitation.
It proposed aggravated trafficking and aiding trafficking as new offences.
accepted.x: The 2018 Bill proposed new offences including aggravated trafficking and aiding trafficking, and also provided for shelters and rehabilitation. It was passed by the Lok Sabha but later lapsed.
accepted.tq: Test the bill’s substantive provisions separately from its legislative status.
accepted.sec: Trafficking - UNODC report, Palermo Protocol, ITPA, Trafficking of Persons Bill 2018/2021  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the Trafficking of Persons Bill, 2018, consider the following statements:
1. It was passed by the Lok Sabha.
2. It subsequently lapsed.
3. It proposed the National Investigation Agency as the national investigating agency.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The 2018 Bill was passed by the Lok Sabha and later lapsed. The proposal to designate the NIA as the national investigating agency belonged to the 2021 draft Bill.
accepted.tq: Separate closely related legislative proposals by year and avoid transferring a feature from one draft to another.
accepted.sec: Trafficking - UNODC report, Palermo Protocol, ITPA, Trafficking of Persons Bill 2018/2021  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The 2021 draft Bill relating to trafficking proposed which agency as the national investigating agency?
accepted.x: The 2021 draft Bill proposed the National Investigation Agency (NIA) as the national investigating agency for trafficking-related matters.
accepted.tq: Use the agency-name trap among bodies with overlapping law-enforcement roles.
accepted.sec: Trafficking - UNODC report, Palermo Protocol, ITPA, Trafficking of Persons Bill 2018/2021  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The UNODC Global Report on Trafficking in Persons, 2016, observed that victims and traffickers often:
o: have no prior social relationship of any kind
belong to entirely different regions and social backgrounds
belong only to organised international networks
accepted.x: The 2016 UNODC report noted that victims and traffickers often share the same background.
accepted.tq: Recall the precise relationship highlighted in the report without substituting a stronger generalisation.
accepted.sec: Trafficking - UNODC report, Palermo Protocol, ITPA, Trafficking of Persons Bill 2018/2021  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the data cited for trafficking cases, which of the following is correctly matched?
o: NCRB 2024 — approximately 2,183 cases in Telangana only
accepted.x: The cited NCRB 2023 figure is approximately 2,183 trafficking cases. The note separately identifies Telangana as having the most trafficking cases in the NCRB 2024 data.
accepted.tq: Separate approximate figures, years and geographical conclusions instead of merging them.
accepted.sec: Trafficking - UNODC report, Palermo Protocol, ITPA, Trafficking of Persons Bill 2018/2021  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which State was reported to have the most trafficking cases in the NCRB 2024 data cited?
accepted.x: Telangana was reported as having the most trafficking cases in the cited NCRB 2024 data.
accepted.tq: Test the location-specific conclusion rather than the total case figure.
accepted.sec: Trafficking - UNODC report, Palermo Protocol, ITPA, Trafficking of Persons Bill 2018/2021  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 was enacted in the immediate aftermath of the:
accepted.x: The 2013 amendment followed the December 2012 Delhi gang rape, commonly referred to as the Nirbhaya case.
accepted.tq: Use the event-year association and distinguish the context of the 2013 and 2018 amendments.
accepted.sec: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2013 - committee, new offences

accepted.s:
The Justice J.S. Verma Committee report led to amendments to which of the following laws in 2013?
1. Indian Penal Code
2. Code of Criminal Procedure
3. Indian Evidence Act
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 amended the IPC, CrPC and Indian Evidence Act following the Justice J.S. Verma Committee report.
accepted.tq: Check the full legislative set instead of stopping at the most familiar statute.
accepted.sec: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2013 - committee, new offences

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched under the 2013 criminal law amendments?
accepted.x: Disrobing was provided under Section 354B IPC, not Section 354E. Sections 354A, 354C and 354D relate respectively to sexual harassment, voyeurism and stalking.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong statutory pairing among closely numbered provisions.
accepted.sec: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2013 - committee, new offences

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (IPC provision)
a. Section 326A
b. Section 326B
c. Section 354C
d. Section 376E

List-II (offence or punishment)
i. Voyeurism
ii. Death for repeat rapists
iii. Acid attack
iv. Attempt to acid attack

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: Section 326A concerns acid attack, Section 326B attempt to acid attack, Section 354C voyeurism and Section 376E death for repeat rapists.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure statutory pairs and eliminate codes containing a swapped offence.
accepted.sec: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2013 - committee, new offences

accepted.s: Which of the following was introduced by the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013?
o: Removal of punishment for repeat rapists
Abolition of the offence of voyeurism
Reduction of the age of consent to 16 years
accepted.x: The 2013 Act introduced stalking as a specific offence under Section 354D IPC. It also introduced voyeurism, while the age of consent was raised to 18 years.
accepted.tq: Identify the genuine new offence while rejecting reversals of the amendment’s provisions.
accepted.sec: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2013 - committee, new offences

accepted.s: Under the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013, the age of consent was raised to:
accepted.x: The 2013 amendment raised the age of consent to 18 years.
accepted.tq: Use the exact age figure and distinguish it from the recommendation of the Verma Committee.
accepted.sec: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2013 - committee, new offences

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding rape under the 2013 amendment is correct?
o: Rape was confined to penile-vaginal penetration.
Penetration by objects or body parts and oral acts were included, and the minimum punishment was raised to seven years.
The minimum punishment was reduced to five years.
Only consensual acts involving adults were covered.
accepted.x: The 2013 amendment widened the definition of rape to include penetration by objects or body parts and oral acts, and raised the minimum punishment to seven years.
accepted.tq: Test the expanded definition together with the associated minimum punishment.
accepted.sec: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2013 - committee, new offences

accepted.s: The Supreme Court struck down the two-finger test in which case?
o: Lata Singh v State of Uttar Pradesh
Shakti Vahini v Union of India
accepted.x: The Supreme Court struck down the two-finger test in Lillu v State in 2013.
accepted.tq: Match the judicial directive with the correct case name.
accepted.sec: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2013 - committee, new offences

accepted.s:
Which of the following was recommended by the Justice J.S. Verma Committee but not adopted in the same form by Parliament?
1. Criminalisation of marital rape
2. No death penalty for rape
3. Keeping the age of consent at 16 years
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Verma Committee recommended criminalising marital rape, opposed the death penalty for rape and recommended retaining the age of consent at 16. Parliament raised the age of consent to 18 years.
accepted.tq: Separate committee recommendations from the final legislative choices.
accepted.sec: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2013 - committee, new offences

accepted.s: Who among the following was NOT a member of the Justice J.S. Verma Committee as listed?
accepted.x: The listed members were Justice J.S. Verma, Justice Leila Seth and Gopal Subramanium. Justice Ranjana Desai was not among them.
accepted.tq: Use the committee-membership trap by identifying the outsider in a closely related judicial group.
accepted.sec: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2013 - committee, new offences

accepted.s: The report of the Justice J.S. Verma Committee was submitted in:
accepted.x: The Justice J.S. Verma Committee submitted its report in January 2013.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the date of the triggering incident from the date of the committee report.
accepted.sec: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2013 - committee, new offences

accepted.s: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018 was enacted in the context of which cases?
accepted.x: The 2018 amendment followed public concern arising from the Kathua and Unnao cases and was associated with the fast-track court response.
accepted.tq: Link the amendment to its immediate factual context without confusing it with the 2013 background.
accepted.sec: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2018 - context, punishment changes

accepted.s: Which of the following punishment changes was made by the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018?
o: Anticipatory bail became mandatory in rape cases involving minors.
All offences against children were made compoundable.
The minimum punishment for rape was reduced from seven to five years.
The minimum punishment for rape was raised from seven to ten years.
accepted.x: The 2018 amendment raised the minimum punishment for rape from seven years to ten years.
accepted.tq: Test the direction and magnitude of the statutory change rather than the offence name alone.
accepted.sec: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2018 - context, punishment changes

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018:
1. Rape of a girl below 16 years attracted a minimum punishment of 20 years.
2. Rape of a girl below 12 years could attract imprisonment for 20 years to life or the death penalty.
3. Gang rape of a girl below 12 years could attract life imprisonment or the death penalty.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe the punishment changes associated with the 2018 amendment.
accepted.tq: Separate age thresholds and punishment ranges carefully; do not merge the under-16 and under-12 categories.
accepted.sec: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2018 - context, punishment changes

accepted.s: Which time-limit combination is associated with the 2018 criminal law changes?
o: Investigation two months, trial two months and appeals six months
Investigation one month, trial six months and appeals one year
Investigation two months, trial six months and appeals one month
Investigation six months, trial two months and appeals two months
accepted.x: The stated timelines were two months for investigation, two months for trial and six months for appeals.
accepted.tq: Match each procedural stage with its specific time limit instead of relying on one familiar figure.
accepted.sec: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2018 - context, punishment changes

accepted.s: In the cases covered by the 2018 amendment, anticipatory bail was barred in relation to rape of a girl:
accepted.x: The 2018 amendment barred anticipatory bail in cases involving rape of a girl below 16 years.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the specific statutory age threshold from broader child-protection categories.
accepted.sec: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2018 - context, punishment changes

accepted.s: In Laxmi v Union of India (2013), the Supreme Court directed that over-the-counter sale of acid should be made:
o: only against photo identification and a stated purpose
freely available without documentation to adults
accepted.x: The Court directed that acid sold over the counter must require photo identification and disclosure of the stated purpose.
accepted.tq: Apply the regulatory conditions to a retail-sale scenario rather than treating regulation as a total ban.
accepted.sec: Acid attacks - Supreme Court directives, regulation of sale, compensation

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the directions relating to the sale of acid in Laxmi v Union of India?
o: Maintenance of a register by sellers
No sale to persons below 18 years
Sale without recording the purchaser’s purpose
accepted.x: The purchaser’s stated purpose had to be recorded; sale without recording it was not permitted. The directions also included photo identification, a register and prohibition of sale to persons below 18 years.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses a specific regulatory safeguard.
accepted.sec: Acid attacks - Supreme Court directives, regulation of sale, compensation

accepted.s: Acid attack victims were directed to receive at least which amount as compensation, along with free treatment?
accepted.x: Laxmi v Union of India directed that acid attack victims receive at least Rs 3 lakh as compensation and free treatment.
accepted.tq: Recall the statutory-relief figure and distinguish it from nearby compensation amounts.
accepted.sec: Acid attacks - Supreme Court directives, regulation of sale, compensation

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched under the law relating to acid attacks?
o: BNS Section 124 — minimum ten years to life imprisonment; attempt — five to seven years
BNS Section 103 — acid attack; attempt — one year
BNS Section 143 — acid attack; attempt — death penalty only
BNS Section 124 — maximum punishment three years; attempt — seven to ten years
accepted.x: BNS Section 124 provides a minimum punishment of ten years extending to life imprisonment for acid attack, while attempt attracts five to seven years.
accepted.tq: Keep the principal offence, section number and attempt punishment aligned.
accepted.sec: Acid attacks - Supreme Court directives, regulation of sale, compensation

accepted.s: The Supreme Court judgment in Shakti Vahini v Union of India (2018) dealt primarily with:
o: interference by khaps in marriages of consenting adults
the two-finger test in rape cases
accepted.x: Shakti Vahini addressed honour crimes and held that khap interference in marriages of consenting adults is illegal, while prescribing preventive, remedial and punitive measures.
accepted.tq: Match the case with its subject matter and distinguish it from other rights-related judgments.
accepted.sec: Honour crimes - Supreme Court guidelines, Law Commission report

accepted.s: Which earlier Supreme Court decision affirmed the right of adults to marry?
accepted.x: Lata Singh (2006) affirmed the right of consenting adults to marry.
accepted.tq: Arrange the judicial authorities by subject and year to identify the earlier precedent.
accepted.sec: Honour crimes - Supreme Court guidelines, Law Commission report

accepted.s: The Law Commission’s 242nd Report, submitted in 2012, proposed a draft law concerning:
o: abolition of the National Investigation Agency
interference in matrimonial alliances in the name of honour
recognition of trafficking victims as offenders
regulation of private hospitals treating acid victims
accepted.x: The 242nd Law Commission Report proposed a draft law against interference in matrimonial alliances in the name of honour.
accepted.tq: Identify the report’s exact subject rather than a broadly related women’s-rights issue.
accepted.sec: Honour crimes - Supreme Court guidelines, Law Commission report

accepted.s:
Honour killings violate which of the following Fundamental Rights provisions?
1. Article 14
2. Article 15
3. Article 19
4. Article 21
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Honour killings violate Articles 14, 15, 19 and 21, which respectively protect equality, prohibit discrimination, protect freedoms and safeguard life and personal liberty.
accepted.tq: Check the complete constitutional grouping instead of selecting only the most familiar right.
accepted.sec: Honour crimes - Supreme Court guidelines, Law Commission report

accepted.s: Honour killings are prosecuted as murder under which provision of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita?
accepted.x: Honour killings are prosecuted as murder under Section 103 of the BNS.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among nearby BNS section numbers by matching the offence category.
accepted.sec: Honour crimes - Supreme Court guidelines, Law Commission report

accepted.s: The directions in Shakti Vahini v Union of India concerning honour crimes included which three categories of measures?
accepted.x: The Supreme Court prescribed preventive, remedial and punitive measures to address honour crimes and unlawful interference in adult marriages.
accepted.tq: Recall the three-part structure of the judicial guidelines exactly.
accepted.sec: Honour crimes - Supreme Court guidelines, Law Commission report
